config.title: Vet in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: What a vet visit costs in Berlin, why the same visit costs more at night and at weekends, where the 24-hour emergency service is, and when it can wait until morning.

items.q: How much does a vet visit cost in Berlin?
items.a: Vets bill from the national fee schedule, the GOT. A general examination with advice for a dog or cat is listed at €23.62 and can be charged at one to three times that during opening hours, plus 19% VAT. That puts a quick look at **€28 to €84**. Medicine, lab work and any extra treatment are billed on top.

items.q: Why is a vet more expensive at night or at the weekend?
items.a: In the emergency service, which covers nights from 18:00 to 08:00, weekends from Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00 and public holidays, the fee range moves to **two to four times** the listed fee and a flat **€50 emergency fee** is added once per case. A quick look at a dog or cat then costs about €116 to €172 including VAT.

items.q: Does a late appointment at my own vet count as the emergency service?
items.a: No. The night and weekend rules do not apply during a practice’s regular consultation hours. If your vet is open until 20:00, a visit at 19:30 is billed at normal rates, and the same goes for a regular Saturday morning surgery.

items.q: Where is the vet emergency service in Berlin?
items.a: The Tierärztekammer Berlin lists five clinics and practices with a 24-hour small-animal emergency service: Klinik für Klein- und Heimtiere in Biesdorf, Valera in Zehlendorf, Tierarztpraxis Bärenwiese in Wilmersdorf, Tierarztpraxis Rödiger in Reinickendorf and VetZentrum Berlin in Marzahn. Call ahead, because animals are seen by urgency.

items.q: When should I go to an emergency vet straight away?
items.a: Go now if your animal has trouble breathing, is bleeding heavily, has collapsed or is having a seizure, has eaten poison, bait, chocolate, grapes or medicine, is a dog with a swollen belly retching without bringing anything up, or is a cat straining without producing urine. For anything else, a phone call first usually tells you whether it can wait.

items.q: Are public holidays billed as emergency time in Berlin?
items.a: Yes, for the whole day. The next Berlin holidays are 3 October, 25 and 26 December and 1 January, and 8 March is a public holiday in Berlin but not in most of Germany. 31 October is a holiday in Brandenburg but a normal day in Berlin.
